Description: The recalled electric fans, which have the brand name "Lollipop" printed on the fan blade cover, have model numbers V1185, V1186, V1865 and V1783, which can be found on the motor housing. The V1185, V1186, and V1865 models have labels that read, "Hi Velocity Lollipop Air Circular." The three-speed, four-position fans are either floor mounted or table top units. The model V1783 has a clip-on base.
Title: CPSC, Brooklyn Lollipop Announce Recall of Electric Fans
ConsumerContact: For more information, call Brooklyn Lollipop collect at (718) 388-9526 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Brooklyn Lollipop have not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Discount and variety stores in the metropolitan New York area sold these electric fans, from May 2000 through July 2002, for between $10 and $15.

Importers.Name: Brooklyn Lollipop Imports and Exports, Inc., of Brooklyn, NY

Hazards.Name: These electric fans have undersized wiring, use a power plug that is not polarized, have an improperly sized grill, and overheat, all of which could cause electrocution, electric shock, fire, and finger entrapment hazards to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these electric fans immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund. Consumers also can return the fans to the firm for a full refund, by mailing the unit to: 7 Marcus Garvey Blvd., Brooklyn, NY 11206.

Description: The recalled stoves include the Century, Hillary, and LL Bean brand names. The stoves have a drip tray, two or three burners, and a black or green base, with a label identifying the brand name. The manufacturing date (050202 through 073102) and model number (4660, 4665, 4675, 4730, 4960, 72861, and 4960LLB) are printed on the inside of the stove's lid.
Title: CPSC, Century Tool and Manufacturing Announce Recall of Camping Stoves
ConsumerContact: The firm that announced the recall is no longer in business. Consumers should contact the previous owner at campstoverecall@gmail.com

Injuries.Name: Century Tool and Manufacturing has received eight reports of hoses separating from the stove, causing one minor injury.

Manufacturers.Name: Century Tool and Manufacturing Co. Inc., of Cherry Valley, Ill.

Retailers.Name: Sporting goods, camping supply and mass merchandise stores nationwide sold these stoves, from May 2002 through September 2002, for up to $90.

Hazards.Name: The burner assembly in the stoves can restrict the flow of gas, which can cause a leak. The leaking gas can ignite and weaken the hose, causing it to separate from the stove and pose a fire hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: The firm that announced the recall is no longer in business. Consumers should stop using the product immediately and contact the previous owner to arrange for returning the product and receiving a refund.

Description: The recalled wooden vehicles include a red wagon, truck and train and were packaged with candy. The following UPC codes are located on the bottom of the vehicles: 694405900012 (wagon), 694405900029 (truck), and 694405900036 (train).
Title: CPSC, Kmart Corp. Announce Recall of Wooden Toy Vehicles
ConsumerContact: For additional information, consumers can contact Kmart at (800) 63KMART anytime or log on to the company's website at www.kmart.com

Injuries.Name: Kmart has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Kmart stores nationwide sold these wooden vehicles, from November 2002 through December 2002, for about $5.

Distributors.Name: Kmart Corp., of Troy, Mich.

Hazards.Name: These products may be given to children as toys. The wheels on the wooden toys may break off into small parts, which may pose a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take them away from children immediately and return them to any Kmart store for a full refund.

Description: The recalled Revel B-15 subwoofers have an outer cabinet with a black or gray speaker grill on the front and are about 20 inches in width, height, and depth. The brand name "Revel" is printed on the bottom left of the rear panel and "PERFORMA B15 SUBWOOFER" is printed on the bottom right.
Title: CPSC, Madrigal Announce Recall of Subwoofers
ConsumerContact: Consumers should immediately contact the dealer from whom the subwoofer was purchased or Madrigal at (800) 424-8043 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to receive a free repair and new computer software. Consumers also can visit the company's website at www.revelspeakers.com

Injuries.Name: Madrigal has received one report of electric shock; though, no injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Madrigal Audio Laboratories, Inc., of Middletown, Conn.

Retailers.Name: Specialty audio dealers sold the subwoofers nationwide and in Puerto Rico, from January 2001 through October 2002, for about $3,000.

Hazards.Name: A screw inside of the subwoofer can cause a high voltage short, which could cause a severe injury to consumers, through an electric shock.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should not touch the rear panel, use the power switch, or remove the power cord or any connections from the back of the unit until it is repaired.

Description: The recalled candles have a clear plastic holder and were available in red, white and green. Some of the candles have the words, "Merry Christmas," "Christmas Morning," "Candy Cane," or "A Christmas Avenue" on the packaging.
Title: CPSC, Atico International Announce Recall of Christmas Candles
ConsumerContact: The firm is out of business. Consumers should call the CPSC hotline at 800-638-2772 (TTY 301-595-7054).

Injuries.Name: Atico has received one report involving melting of the plastic holder; however, no injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Eckerds, Kerr Drugs, Snyders Drugstore, and Farmacias El Amal stores nationwide sold the candles, from September 2002 through December 2002, for between $2.50 and $4.

Importers.Name: Atico International USA Inc., of Fort Lauderdale, Fla.

Hazards.Name: The wick is not properly set inside the tealight, which may cause the plastic holder to melt and pose a fire hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: The firm is out of business, the remedy is no longer available, and the product should be discarded or destroyed.

Description: The recalled sparklers were packaged in a red, white and blue cardboard box and sold with six sparklers per box. Three models of sparklers were sold, including model SP08 measuring 8 inches long, model SP14 measuring 14 inches long, and model SP20 measuring 20 inches long. Labels on the packaging read in part "BAMBOO GOLD SPARKLERS," "6 PIECES," and "MADE IN CHINA."
Title: CPSC, Elkton Sparkler Announce Recall of Bamboo-Stick Sparklers
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Elkton Sparklers at (800) 322-3458 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.easylite.com

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Elkton Sparkler have received four reports of burns and clothing igniting. Injuries include a 6-year-old girl, who received second-degree burns to her ankle, and a 3-year-old boy, who received a minor burn to his leg when his sweat pants caught on fire.

Retailers.Name: Variety Stores sold these sparklers nationwide, from January 2002 through May 2002, for between $2 and $5 a box.

Importers.Name: Elkton Sparkler Company Inc., of North East, Md.

Hazards.Name: The sparklers' bamboo-stick handles can catch fire, burn and disintegrate and emit burning fragments during use. The sparklers present a fire hazard and a risk of burn injury.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these sparklers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

Description: The recall includes the First Moments- or Second Step-brand two-piece pants set. The brand name is written on a label inside the tops of the set. The set's pink fleece top has two patch pockets and the cotton pants have a pink floral print. The set came in sizes 3 months to 24 months. The set has a cut-out floral pattern in the fabric at the end of the sleeves, along the hem of the top and along the top of each pocket. The part of the fabric subject to the cutting has been weakened and tears easily from the rest of the garment.
Title: CPSC, Kohl's Department Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Fleece Pant Sets
ConsumerContact: For more information, call Kohl's toll-free at (800) 694-2647 between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CT Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.Kohls.com

Injuries.Name: Kohl's Department Stores Inc. has received two reports of young children putting torn pieces of fabric in their mouths. One child reportedly began to choke on a piece of material.

Retailers.Name: Kohl's Department Stores sold the pant set nationwide, from September 2002 through early November 2002, for about $18.

Distributors.Name: Kohl's Department Stores Inc., of Menomonee Falls, Wis.

Hazards.Name: Small pieces of fabric at the end of the sleeves, along the hem and on the pockets of the tops can be torn off easily, posing a choking hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the set immediately and return it to the store where purchased for a refund.

Description: This recall includes the "Talking Learn n' Play" dolls with buttons. The dolls describe the functions of zippers, buttons, snaps and shoelaces. The dolls are about 13 inches tall and are dressed in pink jumpers with pink and white plaid shirts. The purple packaging reads, "Talking Learn n' Play."
Title: CPSC, Lovee Doll & Toy Co., Inc. Announce Recall of Talking Dolls
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Lovee Doll & Toy Co., Inc. at (212) 242-1545 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Lovee Doll and Toy Co., Inc. has not received any reports of incidents involving these dolls. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

Retailers.Name: Toy and discount department stores sold the dolls nationwide, from June 2002 through December 2002, for between $10 and $15.

Importers.Name: Lovee Doll and Toy Co., Inc., of New York, N.Y.

Hazards.Name: Buttons on the dolls' outfit could detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these dolls away from children immediately and return the dolls to the store where it was purchased for a refund.

Description: The recall involves the Pumpkin and Snowman model motion lamps. The ceramic lamps have liquid-filled globes that become warm and the heat moves the glitter inside. The Pumpkin lamp has orange liquid in its globe, straw hair and a burlap hat. The Snowman wears a black top hat and a red and black scarf. The Snowman's globe is filled with a clear liquid. On the bottom of each lamp is a sticker that reads, "Made in China."
Title: CPSC, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® Announce Recall of Motion Lamps
ConsumerContact: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® at (888) 645-6516 between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m. ET Monday through Friday. For more information, consumers can log on to the company's web site at www.crackerbarrel.com

Injuries.Name: There have been no reports of incidents or injuries. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

Retailers.Name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Stores® sold the motion lamps nationwide, from August 2002 through October 2002, for about $20.

Importers.Name: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store®, of Lebanon, Tenn.

Hazards.Name: Wires near the light's socket can become exposed, posing a risk of electric shock or electrocution to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using and unplug these lamps immediately and contact Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® to receive a full refund.

Description: The recalled garments were sold under the "Joe Boxer" brand name in sizes 12-months through 18-months and size 24-months. The garments were sold as sets that include a light tan sweat jacket with the word "Smile" embroidered on the front and a painted "smiley face" yellow zipper-pull and red sweat pants. Only style numbers 40801002 and 40801003 are included in the recall and can be found on the reverse side of the care label. Writing on the collar label includes "MADE IN/HECHO EN CHINA."
Title: CPSC, Wear Me Apparel Corp. Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garments
ConsumerContact: For additional questions, consumers can contact Wear Me Apparel Corp. at (212) 842-6172.

Injuries.Name: Wear Me Apparel Corp. and CPSC have not received any reports of injuries involving these garments. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

Retailers.Name: Kmart stores nationwide exclusively sold these garments, from August 2002 through October 2002, for between $10 and $13.

Importers.Name: Wear Me Apparel Corp., of New York, N.Y.

Hazards.Name: The paint on the "smiley face" zipper-pull attached to the sweat jacket of these garments contains lead. Young children could ingest lead from the zipper-pull, presenting a lead poisoning hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should return the clothing sets to any Kmart store to receive a full refund.

Description: The recall includes bunny toys that measure about 10 inches tall and have jackets that button up the front. Some of the jackets, pants and hats on the bunnies have a multi-colored striped or a patterned print. "Zutano" is printed on a tag attached to the bunny. "Hip Hoppy" is printed on a hang tag attached to the bunny. Only bunny toys with buttons are included in the recall.
Title: CPSC, Zutano Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Bunny Toys
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Zutano at (800) 287-5139 between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Zutano has not received any reports of injuries relating to these stuffed bunny toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Department and specialty stores nationwide sold the recalled bunny toys, from July 2000 through December 2002, for about $18.

Importers.Name: Zutano Inc., of Cabot , Vt.

Hazards.Name: The buttons on the front of the bunny's jacket can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these recalled bunny toys away from young children immediately and contact Zutano Inc. to receive a replacement outfit.

Description: The recall involves 7 1/4-inch circular saws with the model number 5740NB. The model number is located on the silver nameplate next to the name "Makita." The saw's housing is blue-green and the name "Makita" appears on the metal blade guard and silver nameplate on the motor housing. Any 5740NB circular saws with an "N" preceding the serial number on the nameplate and a blue dot on the shipping carton are not involved in this recall.
Title: CPSC, Makita U.S.A. Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Circular Saws
ConsumerContact: For more information on how to return the saw or to locate the nearest Makita factory service center, consumers should contact Makita U.S.A. Inc. at (800) 462-5482 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Makita U.S.A. Inc. has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial suppliers nationwide sold the circular saws, from April 1998 to November 2002, for between $99 and $119.

Importers.Name: Makita U.S.A. Inc., of La Mirada, Calif.

Hazards.Name: The lower blade guard of the saw can become jammed, which can result in the consumer coming in contact with the blade and suffering a serious injury.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the circular saws immediately and return them to the nearest Makita factory service center for a free repair.

Description: The recall includes the 15-Amp grinders that have a seven or nine inch disc and have the following catalog and serial numbers, which can be found on a nameplate on the top of the grinder: Catalog Numbers Serial Numbers 6086-20 Serial Prefix 991A and 991B only 6088-20 Serial Prefix 994A and 994B only 6089-20 Serial Prefix 992A
Title: CPSC, Milwaukee Tool Corp. Announce Recall of Electric Grinders
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Milwaukee Electric Tool at (800) 414-6527 between 6 a.m. and 6:30 p.m. CT Monday through Friday. Consumers can locate the nearest service center by visiting the firm's web site at www.heavydutytool.com (the recall announcement on their site can be found at www.milwaukeetools.com/pdfs/15-amp-grinder-recall.pdf).

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Milwaukee Electric Tool have received 12 reports of grinder switches sticking in the "on" position; however, no injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Milwaukee Electric Tool Corp., of Brookfield, Wis.

Retailers.Name: Home centers, hardware stores and industrial distributors nationwide sold these grinders, from June 2001 through November 2002, for between $165 and $175.

Hazards.Name: The grinder's switch can stick in the "on" position, which could pose an injury hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the grinders immediately and return them to their nearest Milwaukee factory service center or authorized power tool service center, for a free repair.

Description: The disposable cigarette lighters being recalled are oval-tube-shaped "BIC" and mini- "BIC" brand lighters. The lighters have a green, red, blue, black or yellow body and a metal top. "BIC" and "Made in France" are imprinted into the metal top of the lighter. A label on the lighter reads, "WARNING KEEP AWAY FROM CHILDREN." The recalled lighters are not equipped with a metal shield over the spark wheel. The child-resistant lighters have that shield. The recalled standard size lighters have the UPC number "3 086120 600020" and the mini-lighters have the UPC number "3 086120 600051."
Title: CPSC, Montrose Wholesale Candies & Sundries Inc. Announce Recall of Illegally Imported Cigarette Lighters
ConsumerContact: For more information, call CPSC's Hotline at (800) 638-2772 anytime.

Images.Caption: A recalled lighter without a child-resistant mechanism

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Montrose Wholesale Candies and Sundries are not aware of any injuries involving these lighters. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Convenience, gas, and grocery stores in the central U.S. sold these disposable cigarette lighters, from September 2002 through December 2002, for about $1.

Importers.Name: Montrose Wholesale Candies and Sundries Inc., of Chicago, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.

Description: These Model HD2420 units have a white plastic enclosure and measure 11 inches wide, 11 inches long and 4 and 1/2 inches tall. "Philips" and "3 in 1" are written on the top of the lid and "MODEL HD2420" can be found on a label on the bottom of the unit. Units marked "Revision A" are not included in this recall.
Title: CPSC, Philips Announce Recall 3-in-1 Waffle Maker/Sandwich Maker/Grill
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Norelco toll free at (800) 243-7884 7:00 am to 9:00 pm (ET) Monday to Friday and 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Saturday and Sunday. Consumers can visit the firms' web site at www.philips.com

Injuries.Name: There has been one report overseas of the sandwich plate contacting an internal wire, which did not result in a shock or injury. No incidents or injuries have been reported in the United States.

Retailers.Name: Target Stores sold this product, from September 2002 to October 2002, for about $50.

Importers.Name: Philips Electronics North America Corp., through its Norelco Consumer Products Company division, of Stamford, Conn.

Hazards.Name: The hinges of the sandwich plate can contact an internal wire, creating a risk of shock or electrocution.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled 3-in-1 Waffle Maker/Sandwich Maker/Grill immediately, unplug it, and return the product to Target Stores for a full refund.

Description: The tent set consists of an "igloo," "tee pee," and connecting tunnel. Only the connecting tunnel is being recalled. They are mostly red, blue and yellow. The modified tunnel has a separate tag that reads: "REPLACEMENT TUNNEL."
Title: CPSC, The Lakeside Collection Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact The Lakeside Collection toll-free at (866) 847-4327, 7:30 am to 4:00 p.m. CST or visit their web site at www.lakeside.com

Products.Name: Kid's Tent Set (only the tunnel is recalled)

Injuries.Name: There have been no injuries.

Retailers.Name: The tent sets were sold by The Lakeside Collection, from May 2002 through November 2002, for about $23.

Distributors.Name: The Lakeside Collection, of Lincolnshire, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact The Lakeside Collection to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by The Lakeside Collection.

Description: This recall involves "Cometa" green and white plastic stack chairs. UPC numbers 0-82294-319754 (white) and 0-82294-319785 (green) are located on a label on the front of the chair. "Made in Italy" and "Not Recommended for Use on Polished or Smooth Surfaces" are also printed on the label.
Title: CPSC and S.I.T. Announce Recall of Plastic Stack Chairs
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact S.I.T. toll-free at (800) 611-4664 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: S.I.T. has received two reports of the chairs collapsing. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Drug stores sold the plastic stack chairs nationwide, from April 2000 through September 2002, for between $4 and $6.

Importers.Name: S.I.T. Inc., of Quincy, Mass.

Hazards.Name: The chairs can collapse during use, causing the consumer to suffer injuries from falls.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these plastic chairs immediately and contact S.I.T. to receive a refund.

Description: The recalled tea lights are packaged 12 candles per box with "Home Interiors" written on the top of the box. Each tea light candle has a clear plastic base and is either red or ivory in color.
Title: CPSC, Home Interiors and Gifts Announce Recall of Tea Lights
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Home Interiors at (972) 695-1085 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Home Interiors and Gifts has received 22 reports of the tea lights flaring up and melting their plastic holders. These incidents have resulted in minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Home Interiors' direct sales associates exclusively sold the recalled tea lights, from September 2002 through November 2002, for about $5 per box.

Importers.Name: Home Interiors and Gifts Inc., of Carrollton, Texas

Hazards.Name: Flames from the tea lights can flare, and the excessive heat can cause the plastic holders to melt, posing a fire hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the tea lights immediately and return any unused tea lights by mail to Home Interiors at 2901 Trade Center Drive, Suite 100, Carrollton, TX 75007. Consumers should include their return address information to receive a retail gift certificate from Home Interiors, for the full purchase cost and shipping cost of the tea lights.

Description: The tent set consists of an "igloo," "tee pee," and connecting tunnel. Only the connecting tunnel is being recalled. They are mostly red, blue and yellow. The modified tunnel has a separate tag that reads: "REPLACEMENT TUNNEL."
Title: CPSC, LTD Commodities, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact LTD Commodities, Inc. toll-free at (866) 736-3654, 7:30 am to 4:00 pm CST or visit their web site at www.ltdcommodities.com

Injuries.Name: LTD Commodities, Inc received one report, in which a child's leg was cut, requiring nine stitches.

Retailers.Name: The tent sets were sold by LTD Commodities, Inc., from May 2002 through November 2002, for about $23.

Distributors.Name: LTD Commodities, Inc., of Bannockburn, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible lacerations.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact LTD Commodities, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by LTD Commodities, Inc.

Description: Oceanic CDX first stage regulators subject to the recall have serial numbers 9200001 to 9205622, 9800013 to 9801711, 0200001 to 0213294, 0D0001 to 0D3046, or 9D0001 to 9D3273. The serial number is stamped into the side of the body of the regulator. The regulators have the name "OCEANIC" written on the rubber boot of the first stage. These CDX regulators were sold with the following second stage regulators: Alpha 7, Delta 3, Gamma 2, and Zeta.
Title: CPSC, Oceanic USA Announce Recall of Scuba Regulators
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Oceanic toll-free at (866) 723-2642 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday, by visiting the firm's web site at www.OceanicWorldWide.com, by writing an email to service@oceanicusa.com, or by writing to Oceanic USA, 2002 Davis Street, San Leandro, CA 94577.

Injuries.Name: Oceanic has received six reports of noise or vibration accompanied by air leakage. No injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Oceanic USA, of San Leandro, Calif.

Retailers.Name: Authorized Oceanic dealers sold these regulator sets worldwide, from May 1999 through October 2002, for between $330 to $640, depending on the second stage.

Hazards.Name: Extreme vibration can occur within these CDX regulators, which can cause an air leakage underwater. Divers could run out of air and drown.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled CDX regulators immediately and take them to any authorized Oceanic dealer to get a free repair. Other repairs or normal maintenance performed in addition to the recall repair will incur a charge.

Description: This recall involves three separate garment sets. Two of the garment sets include a newborn and infant dress with sandals. The other includes an infant capri set with sandals. The dresses were sold in either, red and yellow or chambray. Both have decorative items like ladybugs and flowers attached. The capri sets were sold in lime, coral, yellow and purple, with flower attachments around the neckline and on the sandals. The Good Lad logo is printed on a label inside of the garment, along with the words, "Good Lad of Philadelphia." The garments were made for ages 3 to 24 months.
Title: CPSC, Good Lad Apparel Announce Recall of Infant Girls' Garment and Shoes
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers should contact the company toll-free at (877) 599-5530 between 7:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Good Lad has received three reports of incidents involving the decorative items. A child swallowed a decorative ladybug and two others began to choke on decorative flowers. There have been no reports of injury.

Retailers.Name: Department stores sold the infant garments nationwide, from January 2002 through April 2002, for about $15.

Distributors.Name: Good Lad Apparel of Philadelphia, Pa.

Hazards.Name: Small decorative items on the garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these garments and sandals immediately. Consumers should return the garments to the store where purchased to receive a refund.

Description: The recalled engines, which were manufactured in the United States, have model numbers HMSK 80 through 110 and HM 80 through 100, which can be found on the lower left side of the engine housing. The recalled engines also have a date of manufacture code (DOM) between 02175 and 02268 followed by the letter "C", which can be found on the engine identification decal. The HMSK models are 8 to 11 horsepower Snow King® snowthrower engines, while the HM models are 8 to 10 horsepower Utility engines. The power equipment, brand names, and retailers involved in this recall include: Power Equipment Brand Name Retailers/Dealers Snowthrowers Ariens Simplicity Snapper Toro Home Depot, Ariens Dealers, Blaine's Farm, Fleet Simplicity Dealers Snapper Dealers Toro Dealers Chipper-Shredders MTD Yard Machines Mighty Mac Merry Mac Baker, Earthquake Simplicity Menards, Northern Tool, Home Depot Mackissic Dealers Northern Tool Ardisam Dealers Simplicity Dealers Generators Coleman Powermate North Star Menards Northern Tool Pressure Washers Tilton Aqua-Stripper Tilton Hydra Storm Tilton Dealers Hydra Storm Dealers Wheeled Leaf Blowers MTD Yard Machines Home Depot
Title: CPSC, Tecumseh Products Co. Announce Recall of Power Equipment Engines
ConsumerContact: Contact Tecumseh at (888) 271-4048 between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m. ET Monday through Friday to schedule a free engine repair. Consumers also can log on to the company's website at www.tecumsehpower.com

Injuries.Name: Tecumseh has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Manufacturers.Name: Tecumseh Products Co., Tecumseh, Mich.

Retailers.Name: Products equipped with the recalled engines were sold by retailers and dealers nationwide, from June 2002 through November 2002. Sears, Roebuck & Co. distributed a limited quantity of these recalled products under its Craftsman brand name.

Hazards.Name: A misrouted fuel line in the engine can become damaged, allowing gasoline to leak out, posing a fire hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the power equipment immediately and contact Tecumseh to schedule a free engine repair.

Description: The tent set consists of an "igloo," "tee pee," and connecting tunnel. They are mostly red, blue and yellow.
Title: CPSC, abc Distributing, Inc. Announce Recall of Kid's Tent Set
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact abc Distributing, Inc. by email at tentset@abcdistributing.com or by phone at (305) 944-6971 (Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 5:00 pm).

Injuries.Name: abc Distributing, Inc. has received three reports, two with minor injuries, as a result of the tip of the wire becoming exposed.

Retailers.Name: The tent sets were sold by abc Distributing, Inc., from March 2002 through June 2002, for about $23.

Distributors.Name: abc Distributing, Inc., of North Miami, Fla.

Hazards.Name: The tip of the wire that forms the frame for the connecting tunnel can become exposed, resulting in possible laceration injuries.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the tent set and contact abc Distributing, Inc. to obtain instructions on how to return the connecting tunnel for a replacement, at no charge. All consumers who purchased these tent sets were notified about the recall directly by abc Distributing, Inc.

Description: These 2002 and 2003 model year ATVs have "Cannondale" and "Cannibal" on both sides of the bodywork. "Cannondale" appears on the rear fenders and bodywork of the vehicle; "Cannibal" appears roughly inboard of the operator's knee location.
Title: CPSC, Cannondale Corp. Announce Recall of ATVs
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Cannondale toll free at (877) 357-6686 between 9 a.m. and 8 p.m ET Monday through Friday, between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. ET Saturday, and between 1 p.m. and 5 p.m. ET Sunday.

Injuries.Name: Cannondale Corp. has received 11 reports of these front shocks breaking apart. One consumer has suffered a broken leg.

Manufacturers.Name: Cannondale Corp., of Bethel, Conn.

Retailers.Name: Cannondale dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from February 2002 through September 2002, for $7,000.

Hazards.Name: The front shocks can break apart internally while riding. If this happens, the shock halves can separate, causing the ATV suspension to fail. The operator can lose control of the ATV, possibly resulting in injury or death.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop riding these ATVs and contact their local Cannondale dealer to schedule an appointment to have the front shocks replaced for free.

Description: The recalled ATVs are model number TRX650FA. They are red or olive green and "Rincon" is written on the side cover, with VIN numbers ranging from 478TE280*3A000041 to 478TE280*3A006105. The VIN numbers are located on the left-front frame tube.
Title: CPSC, Honda Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)
ConsumerContact: To locate their local dealer or for more information, consumers should call American Honda at (800) 578-3543 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday or go to the company's web site at www.hondamotorcycle.com

Injuries.Name: Honda has received one report of a bolt falling out and a front suspension collapsing on one of these vehicles. No injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: American Honda Motor Co. Inc., of Torrance Calif.

Retailers.Name: Honda motorcycle dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from July 2002 through October 2002, for approximately $7,000.

Hazards.Name: Vehicle Accident

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these ATVs immediately and call their local Honda ATV dealer to schedule a free repair. Consumers should not attempt to torque these bolts themselves because this job requires shop equipment and special tools not generally available to consumers. Registered owners of the vehicles have been notified directly by American Honda.

Description: This recall involves "Trend Swing" stationary infant swings, model numbers 8711 and 8722 found on a label on the bottom of the seat. The swings were sold in khaki/gingham and navy/white plaid, and feature a toy bar, song player and timer. "Baby Trend" is printed on the front of the seat's tray and "Trend Swing" is printed on the arm. "Baby Trend" and "Made in China" are also printed on the label on the bottom of the seat.
Title: CPSC, Baby Trend Announce Recall to Repair Infant Swings Sold at Toys R Us
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Baby Trend toll-free at (800) 328-7363 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. PT Monday through Friday. Consumers also can visit the firm's web site at www.babytrend.com

Injuries.Name: Baby Trend has received 10 reports of the screws loosening. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Toys R Us stores sold these swings nationwide, from November 2001 through September 2002, for between $60 and $90.

Distributors.Name: Baby Trend Inc., of Ontario, Calif.

Hazards.Name: A screw on the swing's support arm can loosen or detach, causing the seat to separate and drop to one side. This presents a fall hazard to infants.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these recalled swings immediately and contact Baby Trend to receive a free repair kit.

Description: The recall includes only the 12-inch Sulley with Boo plush dolls. The Sulley doll is a blue monster with purple spots, a tail and horns. Sulley is holding a Boo doll in his right arm. Boo is a little girl with dark hair and small pink ball ponytail holders and rubber bands. Both are characters in the 2001 animated film, Monsters, Inc. Labels on the Sulley doll read, "Disney Store," "SULLEY W/BOO 12"," and "Made in China."
Title: CPSC, Disney Store Announce Recall of Monsters, Inc. Character Plush Dolls
ConsumerContact: For more information, call Disney at (800) 566-3161 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday, or visit their web site at www.disneystore.com

Injuries.Name: The Disney Store has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these dolls and is voluntarily recalling them to prevent future incidents.

Retailers.Name: The Disney Stores nationwide exclusively sold these plush dolls, from July 2002 through October 2002, for about $20.

Importers.Name: The Disney Store, Inc., headquartered in Glendale, Calif.

Hazards.Name: The Boo doll's hair has ponytail holders that could detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately remove and discard the two pink ponytail holders and two rubber bands from the Boo doll's hair or return the item to any Disney Store for a full refund.

Description: The walkers are multi-colored and have either a detachable toy bar or a detachable music center on the tray. On each tray are two 6.5-inch stems with 3.5-inch stars on top. The recalled walkers were sold under the "Tot Rider" and "Carter's" brand names. Tot Rider walkers included in the recall have model numbers 14303-AC, 14303-CC and 14401-OT. The model numbers are printed on stickers located on the inside wall of the base of the walkers. The names "Tot Rider" and "Kolcraft" are printed on stickers attached to the front of the walker. The Carter's model walkers included in the recall have model numbers 14303-LB, 14303-UE and 14304- LJ. The model numbers are printed on stickers located on the inside wall of the base of the walkers. The words "Carter's" and "Music Center" are printed on stickers attached to the front of the walker. Walker models 14303 and 14304 were manufactured from December 2000 through August 2002, and walker model 14401 was manufactured from January 2000 through July 2002. The manufacturing date is printed on the sticker with the model number.
Title: CPSC, Kolcraft Announce Recall of Toy Attachments on Baby Walkers
ConsumerContact: For information on receiving a replacement toy bar or music center toy tray, consumers can contact Kolcraft toll-free at (888) 695-9988 anytime or visit the firm's web site at www.kolcraft.com.

Injuries.Name: Kolcraft has received 15 reports of injuries associated with the exposed sharp edges of the toys' stems. The injuries to children included lacerations around the eyes, eyelids, face and tongue.

Retailers.Name: Discount, department and juvenile product stores sold the walkers with these toys nationwide, from December 2000 through October 2002, for between $20 and $40.

Distributors.Name: Kolcraft Enterprises, Inc., of Chicago, Ill.

Hazards.Name: The flower toys on the baby walker's tray can detach from the stems, exposing sharp edges and posing a laceration hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should remove the detachable toy bars or music center toy trays on these walkers immediately.

Description: The holders are constructed of metal and glass disks and are in the shape of a vertical wave pattern. The tea light candles rest behind the glass disks. The holders are purple and black, yellow and white or green and white.
Title: CPSC, Meijer Announce Recall of Three-Tier Tealight Candleholder
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Meijer at (866) 280-8419, 24 hours a day or on the web at www.meijer.com

Injuries.Name: There have been two incidents of candles flaring. The incidents did not result in injury or property damage. Meijer is recalling the candleholder to prevent injury or property damage.

Retailers.Name: Meijer stores located in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois sold the candleholders, from May 2002 through October 2002, for about $7.99.

Distributors.Name: Meijer, of Grand Rapids, MI

Hazards.Name: The middle candleholder is mounted directly below the top candleholder, which can cause the top candle to overheat and flare. This poses a fire hazard, which can result in a burn injury or property damage.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the candleholder immediately and return it to their local Meijer store for a refund.

Description: These are junior-sized compound Bear Archery bows sold under the model names Warrior and Buckmaster/Warrior. They are camouflaged or black, and "Warrior" or "Buckmaster" decals were included in the packaging to put on the bows.
Title: CPSC, Bear Archery LLC Announce Recall of Compound Bows
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Bear Archery at (800) 342-4751 between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday or write to Bear Archery, LLC, 4600 S.W. 41st Blvd., Gainesville, FL 32608.

Injuries.Name: Bear Archery has received about 200 reports of these bows breaking during use, with reports of seven minor injuries, such as cuts and bruises to the face and chest.

Retailers.Name: Hunting & sporting goods stores, mass merchants and catalogs nationwide sold the bows, from September 2002 through October 2002, for between $75 and $100.

Distributors.Name: Bear Archery LLC, of Gainesville, Fla.

Hazards.Name: The limbs of these bows can break during use, causing impact injuries to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled bows immediately and contact Bear Archery for a free replacement.

Description: The recalled garments are white, with a fuzzy cotton/polyester exterior, and lined with bird's-eye cotton. They are hooded with a snap front and available in sizes 6-12 months, 12-18 months and 18-24 months. These jackets have the UPC codes 024911, 024912 or 024913 on the collar tag.
Title: CPSC, Estyle, Inc. recall Children's Jackets
ConsumerContact: For more information, call Estyle at (877) 378-9537 or e-mail custcare@estyle.com

Injuries.Name: None reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Estyle, Inc. of Los Angeles, Calif.

Retailers.Name: Estyle sold the jackets on their web site, from March 2002 through June 2002, for about $68.

Hazards.Name: The jackets do not meet the Standard for the Flammability of Clothing Textiles under the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the jackets immediately and contact Estyle, Inc. for a full refund.

Description: These Everplore-model M100-12V-12.5A-110 chargers have a blue plastic enclosure and measure 5.5 inches wide, 10.5 inches long and 3 inches thick. "EVERPLORE" and Ni-Zn Battery Charger" are written on a blue and white label on the front of the units.
Title: CPSC, Evercel Announce Recall of Nickel Zinc Battery Chargers
ConsumerContact: Contact Evercel collect at (781) 740-1312 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday

Injuries.Name: There have been three reports of these battery chargers overheating and melting, causing minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Evercel Inc., of Hingham, Mass.

Retailers.Name: Cabella's mail order catalogs and web site sold these battery chargers as part of their Evercel Model MOD100-7C Trolling Battery system, from August 2002 through September 2002, for about $299.

Hazards.Name: Internal electrical components of the battery chargers can overheat, posing a fire hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these battery chargers immediately and discard them in accordance with local laws.

Description: The recall involves Physical Science-brand, heather-gray, hooded sweatshirts with a full-zippered front and "P87" embroidered on the left chest. The sweatshirts come in sizes small through XXL, and have two sewn-in labels: one reads "PHYS.SCI" and the other reads "65% COTTON," "35% POLYESTER," "RN 17730," MADE IN CHINA" and "SEE REVERSE FOR CARE." This recall does not include any other "PHYS.SCI" brand garments.
Title: CPSC, Target Corp. Announce Recall of Men's Sweatshirts
ConsumerContact: For additional information about this recall, consumers can call Target at (800) 440-0680 anytime or visit their web site at www.target.com

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Target are not aware of any injuries involving these sweatshirts. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Manufacturers.Name: Trends Clothing Corp., of Miami, Fla.

Retailers.Name: Target Stores nationwide sold the sweatshirts, from August 2002 through September 2002, for about $25.

Distributors.Name: Target Corp., of Minneapolis, Minn.

Hazards.Name: The fleece fabric on the inside of these sweatshirts fails to meet federal mandatory standards of fabric flammability, because it can ignite readily if exposed to flame, and therefore presents a serious risk of burn injuries, in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop wearing these sweatshirts and return them to the store where purchased, for a full refund.

Description: The multicolored flashlights measure about 6 inches in length, and are made of translucent plastic with a black cord attached at the end. "Halo Burger" is written on the side of the flashlight. "Made in China" is printed on a gold-colored label on the bottom of the flashlight. The two "AA" batteries included with the flashlight are labeled "Spadelove Ultra" and are black with a bronze top band.
Title: CPSC, Halo Burger Announce Recall of Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals
ConsumerContact: For additional questions, contact Halo Burger at (810) 238-1839 ext. 27 at anytime.

Products.Name: Flashlights and Batteries Sold in Kids Meals

Injuries.Name: Halo Burger received two reports of young children, who received minor skin irritation on their mouths from leaking flashlight batteries.

Retailers.Name: Halo Burger restaurants distributed the flashlights as a premium with the kids meals in Genesee and Saginaw Counties in Michigan, from October 2002 through November 4, 2002. The flashlights were sold individually for about $1.50.

Importers.Name: Halo Burger, of Flint, Mich.

Hazards.Name: The "AA" batteries provided with each flashlight can leak, which could cause irritation to the skin. When disassembled, the flashlights also have small parts that can pose a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these flashlights and batteries away from children immediately and return the flashlights and batteries to any Halo Burger restaurant to receive a $5 gift certificate, or discard flashlights and batteries in a safe manner.

Description: The recalled Stihl chain saws include model number MS 170 and MS 180 C with serial numbers 255120848 through 255122797 and 255739074 through 255741150. The name "Stihl" and the model numbers are located on the starter housing. The serial number is printed on the housing near the bumper spikes.
Title: CPSC, Stihl Inc. Announce Recall of Chain Saws
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Stihl at (800) 610-6677 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Stihl has received six reports of fuel leakage. No fires or injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Stihl Inc., of Virginia Beach, Va.

Retailers.Name: Stihl dealers nationwide sold the chain saws, from July 2002 through October 2002, for between $180 and $200.

Hazards.Name: Fuel can leak out of the chain saw's tank, which could cause a fire or injury hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the chain saws immediately and return them to the dealer where purchased, for a free repair.

Description: The school supply sets were sold in 8-inch plastic cases. The sets included the razor knife, pencils, scissors, a ruler, an eraser, a compass, and a tube of glue. Writing on the plastic cases includes "LITTLE WHITE," "LITTLE ARTIST," "GOOD FRIENDS," or "ZHONG BAIO REN." The cases are blue, pink yellow or purple and have pictures of children or animals. These sets were sold in plastic bags with cardboard headers marked "10 PCS SET PENCIL CASE & PENCIL HOLDER," and "MADE IN CHINA."
Title: CPSC, Damo Plus Corp. Announce Recall of Children's School Supply Sets
ConsumerContact: For more information about this recall, consumers should call Damo Plus Corp. collect at (323) 583-8484 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Friday. Consumers also can write to the company at Damo Plus Corp., 4535 E. 48th St., Vernon, CA 90058.

Injuries.Name: Damo Plus has not received any reports of injuries from these pencil sets.

Retailers.Name: Discount and dollar stores in California, Texas, Washington, and Maryland sold the sets, between June and October 2002, for about $1.

Importers.Name: Damo Plus Corp., of Vernon, Calif.

Hazards.Name: The sets contain razor knives, which pose a laceration hazard to children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately take these razor knives away from children and return the pencil sets to the store where they purchased them, for a refund.

Description: The multicolored flashlights measure about 5.75 inches in length, and are made with a metal barrel and a plastic head. They take "C" batteries and have a rotating focusing head. The model number FC230KBP appears only on the reverse side of the package. The words Energizer Kidz Club appear on the head of the flashlight. "Made in China" is written on the base.
Title: CPSC, Eveready Battery Co. Inc. Announce Recall of Kidz Club Flashlights
ConsumerContact: Consumers should contact Eveready at (800) 383-7323 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. CT, Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Eveready has received three reports of the flashlights overheating, including one report of a 4-year-old boy receiving a minor burn to his hand.

Retailers.Name: Discount department and toy stores sold these flashlights nationwide, from April 2002 through October 2002, for about $6.

Importers.Name: Eveready Battery Co. Inc., of St. Louis, Mo.

Hazards.Name: The flashlights can overheat and cause the batteries to leak, posing a risk of burns to children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these flashlights away from children immediately and remove the batteries and contact Eveready for instructions on returning the flashlights and receiving a $12 refund.

Description: The recalled swing seats are made of blue polymer material with "Miracle M" embossed on the topside of the seat and an "M" on the underside, above the date code.
Title: CPSC, Miracle Recreation Equipment Company Announce Recall of Public Playground Equipment Swing Seats
ConsumerContact: Consumers or equipment owners can contact Miracle Recreation Co. at (800) 523-4202 Ext. 635 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.miracle-recreation.com

Injuries.Name: Two children have been injured and received stitches to lacerations on an arm and a leg, from exposed metal on edges of swing seats.

Manufacturers.Name: Miracle Recreation Equipment Company, of Monett, Mo.

Retailers.Name: Miracle Recreation Equipment Company sold the swing seats nationwide, from June 2001 to September 2002, for use on public playground equipment.

Hazards.Name: Metal inserts inside the swing seats can wear through and cause lacerations to children.

Remedies.Name: Owners should immediately stop children from using these swing seats and contact Miracle Recreation Co. for free replacement seats and hardware. If there are already exposed metal inserts on the edges of your seats, immediately take down the seats and chains. Do not leave chains on equipment, as children could seriously injure themselves or others with free-hanging chains. Purchasers were previously sent direct mail notification about this recall.

Description: The recalled ramps include the Rage SSD (model 310937) and Skate Attack SSD (model 312912). The ramps are black and have a sticker with the Rage or Skate Attack logo and name on each side. The four peg holes, used to anchor the ramp, are located on the underside of the ramp in each corner. The ramps are 39 inches long, 28 inches wide and as high as 12 inches.
Title: CPSC, Gen-X Sports Incorporated Announce Recall of Skateboard Ramp
ConsumerContact: For more information on returning the ramps, consumers can contact Gen-X toll-free at (866) 846-4369 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday. Consumers can also visit the firm's web site at www.genxsportsinc.com

Injuries.Name: Gen-X Sports has received one report of the ramp cracking. The user, who was riding a scooter at the time of the incident, fell and broke his collarbone.

Retailers.Name: Discount department and sports stores sold the ramps nationwide, from March 2002 through September 2002, for between $20 and $40.

Importers.Name: Gen-X Sports Inc., of Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hazards.Name: The ramps can crack, causing users to fall and suffer injuries.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these ramps immediately and contact Gen-X to receive a refund.

Description: The recalled hand cycles come in a variety of colors and have "SOPUR" written on both sides of the bodywork.
Title: CPSC, Sunrise Medical Announce Recall of 3-Wheel Hand Cycle
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Sunrise Medical in Germany at 0049-7253-980-340 or by e-mail s.gerster@sunrisemedical.de -- Consumers also can visit the firm's web site at www.sunrisemedical.de

Injuries.Name: Sunrise Medical has received one report, in which the quick release failed and the rider suffered minor injuries.

Manufacturers.Name: Sunrise Medical of Heidelberg, Germany

Retailers.Name: Sunrise Medical dealers nationwide sold these hand cycles, from August 2001 to July 2002, for $3,300.

Hazards.Name: There is a small risk that the quick release axles of the rear wheels do not lock correctly. If the quick release axle is not fully and properly engaged, the wheel could become detached while moving. A detached wheel could result in loss of control of the cycle and potential for serious injury or death, due to a fall or collision with another object.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop riding these cycles immediately and contact their local Sunrise Medical dealer for a free repair.

Description: The recalled lights were made in China and have the model number 8311, which can be found on the package. The blue, red, green, or multi-colored lights are about 17 inches in height and have a curved colored piece of glass (the bulb) that inserts into a black base. When the snake light is turned on it gives off the appearance of "lightning" running through the lamp and into the bulb. "Snake Light" is written on the bottom of the light.
Title: CPSC and Carlisle Co. Announce Recall of Snake Lights
ConsumerContact: Consumers can call the Carlisle Co. at (800) 233-3931 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. PT Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: The Carlisle Co. has received one report of the plastic base melting, though no injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Chuck E. Cheese's restaurants nationwide provided the lights as a redemption prize, from July 2002 through September 2002.

Importers.Name: The Carlisle Co. Inc., of Carson City, Nev.

Hazards.Name: The circuit board in the lamps can overheat and melt the plastic housing, posing a fire or thermal burn hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these lights immediately, unplug them, and return them to any Chuck E. Cheese restaurant for a replacement prize of the same value.

Description: The recalled Halloween ghost candleholders are about 10 inches tall and are made of acrylic. The ghosts are white and hold a small orange pumpkin, in which the tea-light candle sits. Two orange pumpkins are painted along the hem of the ghost. The candleholders were made in China.
Title: CPSC, Kohl's Department Stores Announce Recall of Halloween Candleholders
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Kohl's toll-free at (800) 694-2647 between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. CT Monday through Friday. Consumers can also visit the firm's web site at www.kohls.com

Injuries.Name: Kohl's has received two reports of the candleholder igniting, causing smoke and soot damage to surrounding property. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Kohl's Department Stores sold the candleholders nationwide, from August 2002 through October 2002, for about $17.

Importers.Name: Kohl's Department Stores Inc., of Menomonee Falls, Wis.

Hazards.Name: Flames from the tea-light candle can ignite the candleholder, posing a fire hazard and risk of burn injuries to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the candleholders immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.

Description: The recalled treestands have the following brand names and model numbers: API Hi-Point Cable Cat Climbing Treestand, Model #CC501 and API Buckmaster Grand Slam Climbing Treestand, Model #GS3800BM. The treestands have an olive green frame, camo seats and seatbacks with black nylon cinch straps, and a yellow "WARNING" or "DANGER" label that reads in part, "Safety Restraint Must Be Used At All Times."
Title: CPSC, API Outdoors Announce Recall of Hunting Treestands
ConsumerContact: Call  API Outdoors toll-free at (800) 228-4846 anytime.

Injuries.Name: API Outdoors has received two reports of the treestand's cable breaking, including one person who fell from a tree and suffered leg abrasions.

Manufacturers.Name: API Outdoors, of Tallulah, La., a division of Outland Sports Inc., of Overland Park, Kan.

Retailers.Name: Retailers and distributors nationwide, including Wal-Mart, sold the Cable Cat treestands through mid-October 2002, for about $180 and Cabela's stores nationwide sold the Buckmaster treestands through mid-October 2002, for about $230.

Hazards.Name: A cable that secures the treestand to the tree can break, posing the risk of falls and serious injuries to hunters.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these treestands immediately and call API Outdoors, to receive a free replacement cable.

Description: The baths were sold under the brand name Jason AirMasseur™ and Air-Whirlpool Baths, which is written on the bath's control keypad. They have a serial number located on the underside of the bath that can be viewed by removing the equipment access panel. Consumers must check with the firm to determine if their bath is included in the recall.
Title: CPSC, Jason International Inc. Announce Recall of Air-Whirlpool Baths
ConsumerContact: They should call the Jason Technical Service Department at (800) 255-5766 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.jasoninternational.com

Products.Name: Jason AirMasseur™ and Air Whirlpool Baths

Injuries.Name: Jason has received one report of a fire involving one of these baths, which resulted in minor damage. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Plumbing distributors and kitchen and bath showrooms sold these baths nationwide, from January 2002 through September 2002, for about $3,000.

Importers.Name: Jason International Inc., of North Little Rock, Ark.

Hazards.Name: Air baths release heated bubbles into the water. A heating element on these baths can fail to shut off, posing a fire hazard.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should check their bath's serial number and call to determine if their bath is part of the recall. If a bath is included in the recall, consumers should disconnect the electrical supply to their bath by unplugging the equipment or by switching off the circuit breaker immediately and schedule an appointment for a free repair.

Description: The recalled ATVs are the Suzuki "Eiger" LT- A400FK3 and the "Eiger" LT-F400FK3. They are red or green, and carry the identifications "Suzuki" and "Eiger" on both sides of the bodywork, roughly inboard of the operator's knee location.
Title: CPSC, Suzuki Announce Recall of All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Suzuki at (714) 572-1490 between 8:30 a.m. and 4:45 p.m. PT Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: None reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Suzuki Motor Corporation of Brea, Calif.

Retailers.Name: Suzuki dealers nationwide sold these ATVs, from August 2002 to September 2002, for between $5100 and $5300.

Hazards.Name: Some of the ATVs were assembled with a wire harness that may have broken ground wire strands from an improperly crimped wire splice. Broken ground wire strands could result in electrical open circuits. An electrical open circuit could prevent the tail/stop lamp from illuminating or could cause the CDI-unit of the ignition to not function. If the CDI-unit does not function, the engine will stop running, possibly leaving the rider stranded away from his or her base of operation.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should contact their local Suzuki dealer to schedule an appointment for their ATV to be inspected and repaired.

Description: The recall involves the following bicycle models with medium- and large-sized frames: 2002 Gemini 1000 2003 Gemini 2000 2002 Gemini 2000 2003 Gemini 1000 2003 Gemini 900 The bicycles have "Cannondale" written on the downtube, and "Gemini" and the model number are written on the top tube. The bicycles were sold in various colors.
Title: CPSC, Cannondale Corp. Announce Recall of Gemini Bicycles
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Cannondale at (800) BIKEUSA or visit the company's web site at www.cannondale.com, to find a local retailer.

Injuries.Name: Cannondale has received three reports of frames breaking. One minor injury was reported.

Retailers.Name: Authorized Cannondale retailers nationwide sold these bicycles, from December 2001 through September 2002, for between $2,100 and $3,800.

Importers.Name: Cannondale Corp., of Bethel, Conn.

Hazards.Name: The frames on some of these bicycles have been improperly manufactured, causing too much of the thickest portion of the downtube to be removed. This could cause the frame to break during use, resulting in falls and serious injury to riders.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop riding these bicycles immediately and contact their local Cannondale retailer for a free inspection of their bicycle frame. Consumers with improperly manufactured frames will have a free replacement frame installed.

Description: The recall involves Brother laser printers with model numbers HL-1040, HL-1050, HL- 1060, and multi-function printers with model number MFC-P2000. The model number can be found on the top of each unit and adjacent to the Brother® logo. The printers are beige or putty in color, and all were manufactured in China, with the exception of model HL-1060, which was manufactured in Japan.
Title: CPSC, Brother International Announce Recall of Laser Printers
ConsumerContact: For more information or to determine the location of a local, authorized service center, call Brother toll-free at (866) 236-6835 between 9 a.m. and 7:30 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, or log on to the company's website at www.brother.com/usa

Injuries.Name: Brother has received two reports of overheating and fire, with one of the incidents involving minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Retailers, dealers and office super stores nationwide sold these printers, from June 1997 through December 2000, for between $300 and $700.

Importers.Name: Brother International Corp. (Brother) of Bridgewater, N.J.

Hazards.Name: The printers can overheat, posing a fire hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled printers immediately and bring them to an authorized service center for a free repair.

Description: The recalled ceiling fans include the following models: the Islander series, with model number FP320 and date codes 01-00 through 03- 02; the Louvre series, with model number FP1320 and date codes 01-00 through 03-02; and the Tropicana series, with the model number FP1600 and date codes 12-01 through 04-02. The model number and date codes can be found on the manufacturer's sticker, located just above the motor of the fan.
Title: CPSC, Fanimation Announce Recall of Ceiling Fans
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact Fanimation at (888) 284-8938 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday, or log on to the company's website at www.fanimation.com

Injuries.Name: Fanimation has received four reports of hanger brackets breaking, including three instances where the fan fell from the ceiling. No injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Fanimation Design and Manufacturing Inc., of Lebanon, Ind.

Retailers.Name: Lighting showrooms, fan specialty stores and electrical distributors nationwide sold the fans, from February 2000 through July 2002, for between $550 to $850.

Hazards.Name: The hanger bracket can break, which could cause the fan to fall from the ceiling and seriously injure anyone standing nearby.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the fans immediately and contact Fanimation for a free, easy-to-install backup bracket. Customers will not have to disconnect the fan or remove the existing bracket.

Description: The recalled SNUTTIG Bear Soft Toys are red, yellow, blue and black and are about six inches tall. The bears have a contrasting color on the nose, ears, and feet. The name "SNUTTIG," the model number 700- 371-56, the manufacturer code 17596 and the words "Made in Indonesia" are all printed on the product label.
Title: CPSC, IKEA Announce Recall of Stuffed Teddy Bears
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers should contact IKEA at (888) 966-4532) anytime or visit the company's website at www.ikea-usa.com

Injuries.Name: IKEA has not received any report of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: IKEA stores nationwide sold the bears, from August 2001 through September 2002, for about $2.

Importers.Name: IKEA, of Plymouth Meeting, Pa.

Hazards.Name: The plastic beads inside of the bears could come out of the seams, posing an aspiration hazard to young children, who could inhale the small beads.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these bears away from young children immediately and return them to an IKEA store for a $5 gift card towards another IKEA product.

Description: The bicycle is a 26-inch, 21-speed, dual-suspension men's bicycle with a double-bar, white frame. "Kent" is written on the down tube and head tube of the bicycle. The decal reading "2100DH" or "PRO-X" appears on the top tube near the head of the bicycle.
Title: CPSC, Lida Bicycle Co. Announce Recall of Men's Bicycles
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers should call Kent Bicycles at (800) 451- 5368 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Lida Bicycle and the bicycle distributor, Kent International Inc., of Parsippany, N.J., have received four reports of the frames of these bicycles breaking. Two riders suffered minor contusions and abrasions. The other two riders were not injured.

Manufacturers.Name: Lida Bicycle Co. Ltd., of China

Retailers.Name: Discount department stores in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and Illinois, and independent bicycle shops in New York and New Jersey sold these bicycles, from April 2002 through August 2002, for between $200 and $250.

Distributors.Name: Kent International Inc., of Parsippany, N.J.

Hazards.Name: The frames of these bicycles can break apart, causing the rider to fall and suffer injuries.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop riding these bicycles immediately, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or store credit.

Description: The recalled cordless stapler is silver and black and comes with a black charger and charger base. The stapler, charger, and charger base have the name "Swingline" printed on them. The stapler's model number, 48201, as well as the words "Made in China," are stamped on the battery cover on the bottom of the stapler. If the battery cover has the letter "S" in the upper right corner, then the stapler is not included in the recall.
Title: CPSC, Swingline Announce Recall of Rechargeable Staplers
ConsumerContact: Contact Swingline at (800) 820-6220 between 9 a.m. and 9 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: Swingline has not received any reports of incidents. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Office supply retailers nationwide sold the staplers, from June 2002 through September 2002, for about $75.

Importers.Name: Swingline, a division of Acco Brands Inc., of Lincolnshire, Ill.

Hazards.Name: If a consumer inadvertently releases the spring-loaded staple magazine while holding the stapler close to his/her face, there is a risk of injury from a fully loaded magazine striking a consumer in the face.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using these staplers immediately and contact Swingline for a free replacement.

Description: The recall includes Wood's and Edison model 40-pint capacity dehumidifiers. The dehumidifiers were sold in white (Wood's) and beige (Edison) plastic with the word "Wood's" or "Edison" printed across the control panel. Both models have control knobs for fan speed and humidity level, and a "bucket full" light. The model and serial numbers are written on a label behind the removable water bucket on the front of the unit. The label reads in part, "Wood's" or "Edison" and "Made in Canada." Model Name Model Number Serial Number Wood's WMD40W 08603098 - 08822606 Edison EMD40 08669467 - 08669490
Title: CPSC, W.C. Wood Company Announce Recall of Dehumidifiers
ConsumerContact: The firm is out of business. Consumers should call the CPSC hotline at 800-638-2772 (TTY 301-595-7054).

Images.Caption: Label behind the removable water bucket of recalled dehumidifier

Injuries.Name: W.C. Wood discovered the problem through routine testing. No injuries or incidents have been reported. This recall is being done to prevent the possibility of injury.

Retailers.Name: Independent retailers sold the dehumidifiers nationwide, from March 2002 through June 2002, for between $160 and $190.

Importers.Name: W.C. Wood Company, of Ottawa, Ohio

Hazards.Name: Internal wiring can abrade on metal parts, presenting a risk of electric shock to consumers if the insulation wears through.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the recalled dehumidifiers and destroy and discard them. W.C. Woods is out of business. A remedy is no longer available.

Description: The black wire "Scary Tree Tea-Light Holder" is about 18 inches high. The tree branches hold six tea-light candles in orange glass pots.
Title: CPSC, Pottery Barn Announce Recall of Halloween Candleholders
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers should call Pottery Barn toll- free at (800) 699-0449 between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. PT Monday through Saturday, or visit their web site at www.potterybarn.com

Injuries.Name: Pottery Barn has received 10 reports of candles in the candleholder flaring. One consumer reported receiving a minor burn from the candle wax.

Retailers.Name: Pottery Barn stores, web site and catalogs sold the candleholders nationwide, from August 2002 through early October 2002, for about $29.

Distributors.Name: Pottery Barn, of San Francisco, Calif.

Hazards.Name: There have been reports that some tea-light candles burning in the candleholder could flare up, posing a fire hazard and a risk of burn injuries to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the candleholders, and return them to the store where purchased for a refund or exchange. Consumers who purchased the candleholder from the catalog or web site should call to arrange product return and refund, including the cost of postage.

Description: Snapper lawn mowers with model numbers 280922B, 281022BE, LT145H33HBV, and YZ145333BVE are part of this recall. The model number can be found on a white label attached to the top of the lawn mower. Date code 5/02 or 6/02 can be found on the discharge chute.
Title: CPSC, Snapper, Inc. Announce Recall of Riding Lawn Mowers
ConsumerContact: For more information, contact Snapper, Inc. on (800) 935-2967. Monday through Friday 9:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. or at the Snapper web site at www.snapper.com

Images.Caption: Riding Lawn Mower Model No. LT145H33HBV
Riding Lawn Mower Model No. YZ145333BVE

Injuries.Name: None reported.

Manufacturers.Name: Snapper, Inc., of McDonough, Ga.

Retailers.Name: Authorized Snapper dealers sold these mowers nationwide, from May 2002 through June 2002, for between $1,099 to $2,699.

Hazards.Name: The side discharge chute is defective. The material used to manufacture the side discharge chute is not strong enough to prevent projectiles from flying out from under the mower deck, exposing consumers and by-standers to possible injuries from flying debris.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using their lawn mowers until the discharge chute has been replaced. Contact a Snapper dealer immediately for a free replacement.

Description: The recalled ceramic Jack-O-Lanterns are shaped like a pumpkin and are five inches tall, six inches wide, and three inches deep. The tan colored pumpkins have an opening in the back and a straw ribbon attached to the stem of the Jack-O-Lantern. A label attached to the stem of the pumpkin reads, "OCTOBER HARVEST."
Title: CPSC, Target Corp. Announce Recall of Decorative Jack-O-Lanterns
ConsumerContact: For more information, call Target at (800) 440-0680 anytime or log on to the company's website at www.target.com

Injuries.Name: Target has received two reports of candles causing smoke and heat at the top of the Jack-O-Lantern, though no injuries or property damage has been reported.

Retailers.Name: Target stores nationwide sold the Jack-O-Lanterns, from September 2000 through October 2002, for about $5.

Distributors.Name: Target Corp., of Minneapolis, Minn.

Hazards.Name: The flame of a candle placed inside the Jack-O-Lantern could ignite the straw ribbon on the outside, posing fire and burn hazards to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should immediately stop using the Jack-O-Lanterns and return them to the Target store where purchased for a full refund.

Description: The recalled electric cook tops were sold under the "Thermador" brand name and have the model number TMH45PS and serial numbers ranging from 82030001 through 82070100. The model number and serial number can be found inside the cook top, under the hinged top. The recalled stainless steel cook tops are 45 inches wide, have four coil elements, and a griddle/grill.
Title: CPSC and BSH Home Appliances Corp. Announce Recall to Repair 45-Inch Electric Cook Tops
ConsumerContact: Contact BSH Home Appliance at (800) 758-1001 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: BSH Home Appliance has received 2 reports of the cooking controls malfunctioning, though no injuries have been reported.

Manufacturers.Name: BSH Home Appliances Corp., of Huntington Beach, Calif.

Retailers.Name: Appliance and specialty stores nationwide sold the cook tops, from March 2002 through September 2002, for between $1,000 and $1,100.

Hazards.Name: The cooking controls are miswired, which can pose a shock hazard to consumers.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the cook tops immediately and contact BSH Home Appliance for a free in home repair.

Description: The recalled pull-along caterpillar is bright red and yellow and was sold under the Plan Toys brand name. The wooden caterpillar is about 7 inches long and is pulled by a nylon string. The caterpillar's antenna are two blue protruding pegs that extend about 1/2 inch from the head. The recalled lot numbers are 0645917, 12142323 and 0724423 and are printed on the inside flap of the packaging. A stamp on the top of the tail end of the caterpillar displays the Plan Toys logo and the words "Made in Thailand."
Title: CPSC, BRIO® Corporation Announce Recall of Caterpillar Pull Toy
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can contact BRIO toll-free at (888) 274-6869 between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m. CT Monday through Friday.

Injuries.Name: BRIO® has not received any reports of injuries or incidents involving these toys. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

Retailers.Name: Specialty toy stores, Internet retailers and mail order catalogs sold the caterpillar toys nationwide, from January 2002 through September 2002, for about $15.

Distributors.Name: BRIO® Corp., of Germantown, Wis., a subsidiary of BRIO AB, of Sweden

Hazards.Name: The antenna on the pull toy can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these caterpillar toys away from children immediately and send them to BRIO® to receive a replacement toy or a refund, including the cost of postage.

Description: There are eight types of stuffed polyester pool animals involved in this recall: crab, duck, frog, octopus, seahorse, shark, turtle and whale. The brightly colored stuffed animals have a sewn-in label that reads in part, "DOLLAR TREE DISTRIBUTION, INC.," "MADE IN CHINA" and "RN# 87254."
Title: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Stuffed Pool Animal
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can call Dollar Tree Stores at (800) 876-8077 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.dollartree.com

Images.Caption: Image of Assorted Stuffed Pool Animals

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Dollar Tree Stores have received one report of the seam ripping, exposing the polyester stuffing and a plastic bag containing foam beads. No injuries have been reported.

Retailers.Name: Dollar Tree, Only One Dollar, Only $1, Dollar Express and Dollar Bills sold the stuffed animals nationwide, from April 2002 through August 2002, for $1.

Distributors.Name: Dollar Tree Stores Inc., of Chesapeake, Va.

Hazards.Name: The seams can separate, exposing the polyester stuffing and foam beads. The foam beads pose a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these stuffed animals away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

Description: There are three types of sponge animals involved in this recall: whales, turtles and fish. The sponge animals are made of soft terry cloth and have suction cups for attaching to tiled or smooth surfaces. The toys have a sewn-in label that reads in part, "DOLLAR TREE DISTRIBUTION, INC.," "MADE IN CHINA" and "RN# 87254."
Title: CPSC, Dollar Tree Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Toy Sponges
ConsumerContact: For more information, consumers can call Dollar Tree Stores at (800) 876-8077 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday or visit the firm's web site at www.dollartree.com

Injuries.Name: CPSC and Dollar Tree Stores have received one report of an eye coming off. No injuries have been reported. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

Retailers.Name: Dollar Tree, Only One Dollar, Only $1, Dollar Express and Dollar Bills sold the stuffed animals nationwide, from May 2001 through September 2002, for $1.

Distributors.Name: Dollar Tree Stores Inc., of Chesapeake, Va.

Hazards.Name: The eyes on the toys can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children.

Remedies.Name: Consumers should take these sponge animals away from young children immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.

Description: This recall includes the "Honey" model baby walker. The walkers are intended for a baby 5 months and older. They were sold in blue, yellow or pink with a padded seat and an activity tray. Model numbers included in the recall are 820, 860, 862 and 802. The model numbers are printed on the seat backs.
